newsitem.title: FRANCE: Several French opinion polls due next week.
newsitem.headline: Several French opinion polls due next week.

text.p: At least three new polls of voters' intentions in the upcoming May/June French parliamentary election will be published next week, while two polls taken before the snap election was called will be released this week, polling organisation officials said on Thursday.

Louis Harris will publish a poll on Thursday at 1400 GMT of French views on the introduction of a single European currency. The poll was conducted on April 18 and 19, before President Jacques Chirac called the snap election.

The French magazine Le Nouvel Economiste said in a statement it would publish a poll, conducted by CSA Institute, in its Friday edition which shows the French are critical of Chirac, saying a president must keep his promises. The poll was conducted on April 7 and 8.
Edouard Lecerf at Louis Harris said it would conduct two polls of voters' intentions next weekend which would probably appear the following Tuesday in French weekly publications.
An official at SOFRES said it would poll voters this weekend and that the results would be published in the French newspaper Le Figaro at the beginning of next week.
The first opinion poll since a snap election was called on Monday, published by CSA Institute late on Tuesday, showed the centre-right coalition would retain power but with a reduced majority.
Futures traders in Paris said there was talk in the market IFOP would be publishing a poll on Friday although no one at the organisation was immediately available for comment.
